title: Closed error taxonomy
description: Every error the Connector may return. The set is closed: a code not listed here is a protocol violation, because a client cannot decide whether to retry an error it has never seen, and a silently-unhandled error in a proxy tool means traffic goes somewhere the user did not choose. `retryable` is the client's whole backoff policy, so it is data, not a comment: every entry declares it as a JSON boolean, an entry that is not an object fails here rather than passing vacuously, and a frame's optional `error.retryable` hint must equal the value declared for that code (scripts/verify.mjs compares every fixture error against this table). `surface` is where the screen shows the code; it is a second closed vocabulary, declared in packages/schema/presentation.json#/errorPlacements/values, because a code whose placement nobody implements is an error the user never sees.

codes.meaning: Frame is well-formed JSON but violates the call contract (missing args, wrong shape).
Method is not in the allowlist. Hard stop, no fallthrough (ADR-0007).

Payload validated against a schema version the receiver does not implement, or a body two or more parsers claim: both are a receiver that cannot name the shape it was handed, and the ambiguous-parse case names every claimant.

no supported intersection between the two ends' declared version windows. `framing.json#/versionFloors` declares two windows and this one code refuses both, because adding a code is breaking for a client that switches exhaustively; today the window that is negotiated is the protocol one, in connector.hello.
Sender extension id is not on the allowlist the host resolved at startup.
A profile or server document failed entity validation.
Semantically invalid transport combination, e.g. xtls-rprx-vision over ws. Rejected rather than silently ignored (docs/architecture/23).
A secret-bearing field was present in a place that syncs or logs. The call was refused instead of stripping it.
chrome.storage.sync or keystore quota hit. Client must fall back and tell the user.
Operation needs a running Core. Call core.start; do not retry blindly.
A second supervisor tried to start Core on the same ports.
Core exited unexpectedly. Triggers the fail-closed path (docs/architecture/30).
Compiled config was rejected by Core. The previous working config stays applied.
A health probe failed. Never used to decide that the proxy is healthy.
TLS/REALITY handshake did not complete. Distinct from HealthCheckFailed so the UI can say what failed.
Server rejected the credential (UUID/shortId). Retrying wastes a probe budget.
No route / DNS failure to the endpoint.
Deadline owned by the caller expired. The Connector may still be working; the caller must treat a late response as discardable (envelope.inReplyTo).
Binary hash or chunk reassembly hash differs from the pin. Core refuses to start (docs/architecture/33).
Cannot write config, keystore or logs.
OS-level secret store inaccessible (e.g. DPAPI call failed, wrong user session).

Single-flight guard: a reconcile is already in progress for this resource, or the sender's rate budget for this class is spent (framing.json senderPolicy.rateLimits). Both mean 'ask again, nothing was lost'.
Unmapped failure. MUST produce a diagnostics record; MUST NOT be the default for anything the caller could handle.
